posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

recentPosts.caption: Could humans evolve to be able to fly some day? Flying like a bird would require way more than just wings. Hollow bones, giant chest muscles, rewired nerves, and absurd amounts of food might allow you to fly, but all of this would transform you into something barely human anymore.

In a battle against cancer, could viruses be our allies? When Croatian virologist Dr. Beata Halassy’s breast cancer returned for the third time, she made a bold decision: to experiment on herself using millions of viruses grown in her own lab. Viruses love cancer cells, which helped her turn them into a weapon against her own tumor.

What happens when you infect cancer with a virus, and could virotherapy become a powerful new tool against cancer? Watch our full video to find out!

What if continents and oceans switched places? The Pacific becomes a supercontinent. Earth's deepest point is Everest Deep, and is almost nine kilometers below sea-level. And the Mid-Atlantic Canyon divides the world from pole to pole. Life finds a way but struggles in this new, upside-down world. This all sounds cool, until the oxygen runs out.

Pigeons are basically GPS Drones with superpowers. They can pinpoint their own location hundreds of kilometers from their roosts and navigate home autonomously, only using smell, the Sun, and even Earth’s magnetic field.

No one works harder than our rover driver Yolk, who is tirelessly collecting nuggets every day so that the space station can function smoothly.

Have you already started your space adventure? Star Birds, which we developed together with our friends at @toukana_interactive, is available on Steam!
Two billion years ago, the world’s first nuclear reactors appeared in Oklo, Gabon. They were NOT made by humans and were self-regulating and accident-free.

In the late 9th century, Vikings have raided kingdom after kingdom and nearly conquered all of England. Wealthy monasteries and defenseless nuns were especially tempting targets and often suffered great losses. However, all of that stopped when Vikings were confronted by princess Aethelflaed, daughter of Alfred the Great.

Who was Lady of Mercia, and how did she shape the history of England by becoming Vikings' greatest nightmare? Watch our latest Nightshift video to find out! 🌚
Laughing gas can make you feel relaxed and euphoric in seconds. But it comes with serious risks as well. So, what exactly is laughing gas and why does it feel so good?

In the 17th century in Germany, one of Europe’s most terrifying witch hunts turned the town of Bamberg against itself. Tortures that occurred in the "Witch Factory" forced innocent people to name friends, neighbors and family members, creating a deadly chain reaction that eventually reached even the richest and most powerful, while those running the trials profited from the people they condemned.

What if you could skip the boring and painful parts of life? It sounds tempting until you realize what you’d lose along the way. Time doesn’t really stop, and neither does the world.
Brace yourself... 😔

We’re working on 12 monthly challenges for our factory-building game Star Birds. And we want to name each challenge after a star constellation!

We’re not looking for the usual suspects like Capricorn, Gemini or Scorpio. We want weird, creative, charming, ridiculous or completely made-up constellations instead.

Got an idea? Drop your constellation names in the comments! Our favorite suggestions might actually make it into the game.

Beautiful family heritage moments. ✈️❤️⁠
Some journeys are about more than the places we travel to, they’re about the traditions, memories, and stories we carry forward.⁠
⁠
A beautiful reminder that the greatest legacy isn’t always something you inherit, but something you keep alive for the next generation. ⁠
🎥: @ajbohannon13

Extremely rare moments with one of the world’s most elusive wild cats. 🐾⁠
⁠
Meet the kodkod, the smallest wild cat in the Americas. Native to the forests of Chile and parts of Argentina, this tiny predator is incredibly difficult to spot in the wild.⁠
⁠
Kodkods are excellent climbers and can hunt both on the ground and in trees. Their paws help them move through the forest, while their long tails provide balance as they climb.⁠
⁠
Because they are so secretive and live in dense forests, sighting

A little pink beauty blending into the wetlands. 🌸🦩⁠
@debsandidge captured a young Roseate Spoonbill in one of nature’s most beautiful stages. Unlike adults, juveniles start out with much paler feathers and gradually develop the vibrant pink coloring they’re known for, reaching their full color at around three years old.⁠
⁠
Even before that transformation, they’re pretty spectacular to look at. ✨⁠

Link in bio to get the list.

Hotels have empty rooms every single night, and they need content constantly. An agency charges them thousands for it. A creator who can film the place properly costs them a room that was sitting empty anyway.

That’s why this works, and why follower count matters far less than people think. One of our members had under 500 followers in May. By August he’d landed over 10 free stays, all filmed on his phone. The luxury properties said yes fastest, it was the smaller

These houses in Romania look like they’re watching you. 👀⁠
⁠
Known as the “Eyes of Sibiu,” these unusual dormer windows appear on the roofs of houses across Sibiu, a historic city in Transylvania.⁠
⁠
The windows come in different shapes, but their eye-like design has given Sibiu its nickname, “The City with Eyes.”

A beautiful hike with one slightly "terrifying" catch… 😅🏜️⁠
The narrow canyons of Utah, where the adventure comes with a very real question: will you actually fit through?⁠
⁠
Some sections are so tight that hikers need to consider their own measurements before taking on the route, making this scenic adventure equal parts breathtaking and nerve-racking.⁠
🎥: @jackie.travel.photos

@garyfive captured these ancient cities that once stood along the ancient Silk Road beautifully.⁠
⁠
Samarkand, Bukhara, and Khiva connected traders and travelers across Central Asia for centuries, becoming important centers of trade, culture, and architecture.⁠
⁠
Today, their grand mosques, ornate madrasas, historic streets, and ancient monuments still tell the story of the Silk Road.⁠

This might be the most fun way to dive into a lake! 🌊😂⁠
A unique spot in Slovenia where a waterslide sends you straight into the lake turning a simple swim into an adrenaline-filled adventure.⁠
⁠
Would you take the slide? ⁠
🎥: @domen_gabrijelicic

Dinner inside a hot air balloon? You can actually do that at Beaverbrook. 🎈⁠
⁠
Set in the hotel’s Italian Garden, six tethered balloons create private spaces for dinner, with a Japanese-inspired menu that includes sushi, sashimi, and Yakiniku.⁠
⁠
The balloons stay on the ground, but the setting is anything but ordinary.⁠
⁠
By: @beaverbrook

A feast by the sea just hits different. 🌊🍽️✨⁠
The perfect combination of fresh dishes, seaside views, and a great presentation.⁠
⁠
Would you order this meal? 👀⁠
🎥: @fricolandia

This lake looks shallow, but it’s actually up to 10 meters deep. 💚⁠
⁠
Paisu Pok Lake sits on Peleng Island in Indonesia’s Banggai Islands and is known for its incredibly clear water. The visibility is so good that submerged trees and parts of the lakebed can be seen from the surface.⁠
⁠
Surrounded by tropical forest, the lake creates an incredible contrast between its dark blue water and lush green surroundings.⁠
⁠
By: @danielkordan

Australia’s hidden underwater treasure. 🌿🐉🇦🇺⁠
The weedy seadragon, a fascinating marine species found only in southern Australian waters.⁠
With its seaweed-like body and delicate appendages, it can almost disappear among the kelp, making it a true master of camouflage.⁠
⁠
And here’s the surprising part: the dads carry the eggs! The female transfers hundreds of eggs to the male’s tail, where he protects them until they hatch.⁠
🎥: @milenus @el.underwater

Meet Agbaibor, a critically endangered African forest elephant. At around eight months old, he was found wandering alone near Nigeria's Okomu National Park, a highly unusual sight since elephant calves typically stay with their mothers until they're weaned at around two to three years old. It's unclear how he became separated from his family, but after being transported to a nearby ranger outpost, he became the first case of elephant rescue in the country.

A new species of cat has been discovered for the first time in a century. When National Geographic Explorer and biologist Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz first encountered the cat at a wildlife sanctuary in Bolivia a decade ago, she thought it belonged to the species Leopardus tigrinus. It wasn't until later that research and genetic analysis showed that the cat had its own distinct place on the family tree—and experts think that there may be more new species of small wild cats to discover around the wo

On safari in the Pantanal, photographer @sandesh_kadur noticed a black vulture in the middle of the water. "I wasn't sure what was going on, so our amazing Boat Guide, Branco, veered towards the vulture. That’s when I saw a dead caiman floating on the water's surface. The single vulture that had landed on it was trying in desperation to feed on the carcass, but the log-rolling caiman proved to be quite the challenge—like trying to eat while on a treadmill."

New cat alert! A call from a wildlife sanctuary about a "weird cat" has led to the first new cat species discovered in over 100 years. Smaller than an average housecat and covered in leopard-like spots, the cat species—proposed name Leopardus tilcayo—lives in Bolivia’s Yungas forest ecoregion, and very little is known about its day-to-day life in the wild.
